title: Organic Chemistry
short_title: naming hydrocarbons, functional groups, isomers and polymers
standard_text: Organic chemistry and its applications have significant implications for human health, society and the environment: hydrocarbons, naming, functional groups, isomers and polymers. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Chemistry 11)
meta_desc: Free Chemistry 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): naming hydrocarbons, functional groups, isomers and polymers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Organic compounds are built on carbon chains.
body_html:
How to think about it

Carbon forms four bonds, so it can make long chains and rings. Alkanes have only single bonds (CnH2n+2), alkenes have a double bond and alkynes a triple bond. Names show the number of carbons: methane, ethane, propane, butane.

Functional groups give compounds their properties: alcohols (−OH), carboxylic acids (−COOH), esters, aldehydes, ketones and amines. Isomers have the same formula but different structures. Polymers are long chains of repeating monomers, such as polyethylene.

Example

How many carbon atoms are in pentane?

pent- = 5

Answer: 5

Example

Which functional group makes a compound an alcohol?

Ethanol has it.

Answer: −OH

Common mistakes

  • Confusing alkanes, alkenes and alkynes.
  • Thinking isomers have different formulas.
  • Numbering the chain from the wrong end.

faq.q: Why are plastics hard to break down?
faq.a: Their long carbon chains are not easily broken by decomposers.

items.q: What type of polymer is Terylene (PET)?
items.e: Made from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid.

items.q: Why does benzene react by substitution rather than addition?
c: benzene is not reactive at all
substitution keeps the stable delocalized ring of electrons
items.e: The delocalized π system gives extra stability.

items.q: What type of isomerism do amino acids (except glycine) show?
items.e: They have a chiral carbon.

items.q: What is the product when an acyl chloride reacts with water?
items.e: Nucleophilic addition–elimination.

items.q: Why are polyesters biodegradable while polyalkenes are not?
c: their ester links can be hydrolyzed
items.e: Polyalkenes have only non-polar C–C and C–H bonds.

items.q: Pentyl butanoate is hydrolyzed. Which acid and alcohol form?
items.e: Split at the C–O bond: the -oate part gives the acid, the -yl part gives the alcohol.

items.q: What gas forms when a carboxylic acid reacts with sodium carbonate?
items.e: This fizzing is a test for carboxylic acids.

items.q: What is the product when ethanoyl chloride reacts with ammonia?

items.q: What is made when propanone is reduced with NaBH₄?

items.q: What is the electrophile in the nitration of benzene?

items.q: What does 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNPH) detect?

items.q: Which reagent reduces nitrobenzene to phenylamine?

items.q: Why do carboxylic acids have high boiling points?

items.q: Which compound gives a red precipitate when warmed with Fehling's solution?
items.e: Aldehydes reduce Cu²⁺ to Cu₂O.

items.q: What is the zwitterion of an amino acid?

items.q: Why is phenylamine a weaker base than ethylamine?

items.e: The lone pair is less available to accept a proton.

items.q: Why is aniline a weaker base than ammonia?

items.e: Resonance reduces electron availability.

items.q: How many moles of oxygen are needed to burn one mole of C<sub>22</sub>H<sub>46</sub> completely?
